question: S007 section 3: WHY DO 28+ GB OF EXPERT WEIGHTS NEED TO BE STORED INDEPENDENTLY? Answered by measurement before spending any implementation effort on a structural class.

probe_1_cross_expert_spectrum.method: Stack a layer's 64 experts as [64, D], centre across experts (so the question is about SHARED structure, not the mean), take the Gram eigenspectrum. 12 probes: layers 1/8/15/25 x gate/up/down.
probe_1_cross_expert_spectrum.NULL_CONTROL: 64 INDEPENDENT gaussian matrices of the same shape give k50=29, k90=56, k99=63, top1=0.0200. The real experts are STATISTICALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE from independent random matrices in shared linear structure.
probe_1_cross_expert_spectrum.VERDICT_KILLS_FOUR_FAMILIES: SHARED EXPERT BASIS, CLUSTERED EXPERT DICTIONARY, LOW-RANK RESIDUAL ACROSS EXPERTS, and CROSS-EXPERT SHARING are all DEAD on arithmetic. Capturing 90% of the centred variance needs 57 of 64 basis vectors, each of dimension 1408x2048; storing that basis plus 64 coordinate vectors costs MORE than storing the 64 experts. The answer to 'why do these bytes exist' is that they are genuinely near-orthogonal information.
probe_1_cross_expert_spectrum.note: This supplies the NUMBER that O003_PROV.json's earlier kill of clustering/low_rank/common_delta was missing, which G014 flagged as the gap.

probe_2_routing_skew.method: Count how often each of the 64 experts is selected, over 1024 real tokens, by hooking the gather indices on all 78 expert tensors.
probe_2_routing_skew.summary: top-8 of 64 take 37.47% of all routing against a uniform 12.5% -- 3.0x concentration. The bottom 32 take 16.61% against a uniform 50%. Max/mean is 5.33x. On average 1.81 experts per tensor are NEVER routed.
probe_2_routing_skew.VERDICT_ONE_FAMILY_SURVIVES: HOT/COLD EXPERT REPRESENTATION is SUPPORTED by measurement. Routing is strongly skewed, so an unequal byte budget across experts has a real basis. This also explains the per-expert calibration result: experts differ because they SEE different amounts and kinds of traffic.

WHAT_THIS_DOES_TO_THE_SEARCH: Of the twelve structural families dispatched to Grok, four are killed by probe 1 before any lane reports, and one is confirmed viable by probe 2. That is the redirection S007 demanded: not more enumeration, but a discriminator that removes families from the space. The surviving structural directions are hot/cold, router-conditioned, sensitivity-weighted, generated, structured factorization (which imposes structure rather than discovering it, so probe 1 does NOT kill it), and the physical rewrite.
CAVEAT: Probe 1 tests LINEAR shared structure across experts within a layer. It does not test nonlinear structure, cross-LAYER structure, or structure in a transformed basis (e.g. after permutation alignment). Cross-layer was not probed here and remains open.
